guard_patterns.handling: Require an accessible official or statutory public source.
Keep publication/update date with the claim.
Keep the measurement/reference period separate from publication date.
Preserve UK, GB, England, country, region, operator or installation scope.
Retain provisional, revised, official-statistics or statistics-in-development status.
Do not convert activity counts or flows into emissions without a compatible method.
Keep counts of meters, chargers, vehicles, holdings or projects distinct from energy quantities.
Keep installed/planned capacity distinct from actual generation or consumption.
Keep planning/project status distinct from commissioned operation.
Keep estimated, survey-based, modelled and measured quantities distinct.
Retain sampling uncertainty and confidence-interval context for survey estimates.
Keep ETS, RTFO and other regulatory eligibility/obligation boundaries explicit.
Keep certificates, allowances and credits distinct from physical fuel or emissions quantities.
Keep installed stock, new installations, annual activity and cumulative totals distinct.
Retain corrections and revision provenance where a series has changed.
Keep pathways, targets and forecasts distinct from observed outcomes.
Preserve units and normalising denominators before comparison or calculation.
Keep exclusions, population coverage and reporting coverage explicit.
No cadastral-parcel emissions value without parcel identity, geometry, compatible activity and method binding.
Every package must pass deterministic structure, scope and provenance checks.

packages.title: Smart-meter installation versus operating-stock QA
facts: DESNZ published the March 2026 quarterly smart-meter update on 28 May 2026.
The release covers smart meters installed by large energy suppliers during January to March 2026.
It also covers total smart and non-smart meters operated by those suppliers at the end of March 2026.
The published series includes quarterly and annual operating and installation counts from 2012 onwards.
Meter installation and operating counts are deployment metrics, not direct energy-consumption or greenhouse-gas measurements.

packages.title: Smart-meter Great Britain geographic-scope QA
facts: The March 2026 smart-meter release applies to England, Scotland and Wales.
The release is explicitly titled for Great Britain rather than the entire United Kingdom.
Geographic scope must therefore be preserved when combining with UK-wide datasets.
A Great Britain deployment total cannot be silently treated as a Northern-Ireland-inclusive UK total.
Geographic coverage does not provide parcel-level meter identity.

packages.title: Smart-meter future-release guard QA
facts: The March 2026 release states that the next quarterly publication for the period ending June 2026 is due on 27 August 2026.
That end-June release is future-dated relative to 24 July 2026.
A scheduled future release must not be treated as already published evidence.
The latest published quarterly smart-meter evidence remains the March 2026 update at this point in time.
Future publication timing does not justify projecting meter counts.

packages.title: Public EV charger July-2026 monthly-indicator QA
facts: The DfT/OZEV charging-infrastructure collection was updated on 8 July 2026.
The collection includes monthly public EV charger indicators by country and region for 1 July 2026.
The monthly indicator measures public charging provision rather than vehicle energy consumption.
Public charger counts do not measure electricity delivered by individual devices.
Public charger infrastructure cannot be converted directly into parcel greenhouse-gas emissions.

packages.title: EV charger quarterly-versus-monthly release QA
facts: The charging-infrastructure collection distinguishes monthly faster indicators from quarterly statistics.
Monthly public-charger indicators and quarterly infrastructure statistics are separate products.
A monthly stock indicator should not be substituted for a quarterly grant-funding measure.
Publication cadence must be preserved when comparing charger series.
Neither cadence supplies parcel-specific charging energy.

packages.title: EV charger public-infrastructure scope QA
facts: The DfT/OZEV collection is about public electric-vehicle charging provision and grant-funded charging.
Publicly available chargers are a different population from all private home or workplace chargers.
Counts by country and region describe infrastructure availability.
Charger availability is not the same as charging sessions or kilowatt-hours delivered.
Public charging statistics therefore require a separate activity source before emissions estimation.

packages.title: REPD April-2026 Q1 vintage QA
facts: DESNZ updated the Renewable Energy Planning Database page on 6 May 2026.
The update replaced the January 2026 files with the April 2026 Q1 extract.
REPD is a monitoring database for renewable-energy projects.
Database vintage must be preserved because project status can change between quarterly extracts.
A project record in REPD is not itself evidence of current generation or emissions.

packages.title: REPD project-status versus generation QA
facts: REPD records renewable-energy project monitoring information.
Planning or development status is different from operational electricity generation.
An operational project entry still does not by itself quantify output during a chosen period.
Project capacity and status require separate generation data for energy-output calculations.
REPD project information must not be interpreted as parcel emissions.

packages.title: REPD site-area geometry guard QA
facts: The REPD update history records work to add site-area information for operational solar projects.
Site area is a project attribute rather than an emissions measurement.
Project site area is not necessarily identical to a cadastral parcel boundary.
Planning-site geometry must not be treated as legal parcel identity without an explicit geometry match.
Area information alone cannot establish greenhouse-gas intensity.

packages.title: Provisional Woodland Statistics 2026 status QA
facts: Provisional Woodland Statistics 2026 were published on 25 June 2026.
The release provides initial estimates rather than final forestry statistics.
It covers woodland area, certified woodland area, planting and Woodland Carbon Code uptake.
The release provides UK and constituent-country statistics.
Provisional woodland metrics must retain their provisional status in downstream QA.

packages.title: Woodland area versus carbon-stock QA
facts: Provisional Woodland Statistics report woodland-area metrics.
Woodland area is not the same quantity as forest carbon stock.
Planting area is not a direct measurement of annual carbon sequestration.
Certified woodland area is a certification metric rather than a greenhouse-gas measurement.
Parcel carbon values require separate carbon-stock or flux methodology plus parcel geometry.

packages.title: Woodland Carbon Code uptake boundary QA
facts: The provisional woodland release includes uptake of the Woodland Carbon Code.
Scheme uptake is distinct from measured carbon sequestration.
Participation in a carbon standard does not by itself state realised annual greenhouse-gas removals.
Scheme statistics must be kept separate from physical woodland-area and carbon-flux metrics.
Woodland Carbon Code uptake cannot be assigned to a parcel without explicit project-to-parcel evidence.

packages.title: Forestry KPI England national-scope QA
facts: The Forestry Commission KPI report for 2025-26 was published on 25 June 2026.
The release applies to England.
The report provides national-level headline and further indicators for Forestry Commission functions.
National KPI values are not site-specific observations.
England-level forestry indicators cannot be downscaled to a parcel without a supported allocation method.

packages.title: Forestry final-versus-provisional vintage QA
facts: Forestry Statistics 2025 were published on 25 September 2025 as a detailed annual compendium.
Provisional Woodland Statistics 2026 were published later on 25 June 2026 as initial estimates for selected woodland metrics.
The two releases have different statistical vintages and scopes.
Final prior-year compendium data should not be silently merged with provisional current-year indicators as one homogeneous series.
Version and release status must accompany any forestry-derived candidate.

packages.title: Agriculture 2025 publication/reference-year QA
facts: Agriculture in the United Kingdom 2025 was published on 9 July 2026 and updated on 10 July 2026.
The publication contains multiple chapters covering structure, livestock, inputs and the environment.
Publication year and the reference years of individual indicators are not always identical.
Environmental emissions in the agri-environment chapter include estimates through 2024.
Reference period must therefore be preserved at indicator level.

packages.title: Agricultural GHG long-run trend QA
facts: Defra's 2025 agri-environment chapter reports estimated agriculture greenhouse-gas and air-pollution emissions.
It states that these emissions fell by 15% between 1990 and 2024.
The reported change is a national sector trend, not a farm-level measurement.
The trend combines a long reference interval and must not be labelled as a 2025 emissions change.
A national sector trend cannot be assigned to cadastral parcels.

packages.title: Agricultural utilised-area activity QA
facts: The 2025 agriculture structure chapter reports UK utilised agricultural area of about 17 million hectares.
It states that this represented about 69% of UK land area.
Utilised agricultural area is a land-use activity metric.
Land area alone does not measure livestock, fertiliser, soil or fuel greenhouse-gas emissions.
Area-based activity requires compatible emissions factors or models before any emissions estimate.

packages.title: Agricultural livestock-count activity QA
facts: The 2025 structure chapter reports cattle, pig, sheep and poultry populations.
The publication reports that total cattle and calves decreased compared with 2024.
It reports that sheep and lamb numbers also decreased compared with 2024.
Livestock counts are activity inputs rather than direct greenhouse-gas measurements.
Farm or parcel emissions require species, management, location and compatible emissions methodology beyond national counts.

packages.title: CAA Q1-2026 aviation-activity scope QA
facts: The UK Civil Aviation Authority provides a quarterly Aviation Trends report for 2026 Q1.
The quarterly material includes flight movements, passengers, punctuality and cargo indicators.
These are aviation activity and service metrics.
Passenger or movement counts do not directly state carbon dioxide or total greenhouse-gas emissions.
Airport activity cannot be attributed to a parcel-level emissions value without an explicit emissions method and boundary.

packages.title: CAA movement/passenger/cargo metric separation QA
facts: CAA quarterly aviation statistics present air-transport movements separately from passengers and cargo.
Each metric has a different unit and denominator.
Flight movements cannot be substituted for passenger counts.
Cargo tonnage cannot be substituted for fuel burn.
Metric separation must be preserved before any emissions model is applied.

packages.title: UK ETS maritime reporting-timing QA
facts: Current UK ETS participation guidance includes maritime emissions reporting obligations.
Maritime operators must submit a verified annual emissions report by 31 March following each scheme year.
The guidance identifies 1 July 2026 as the start of the maritime scheme period used for the first surrender calculation.
Reporting timing and scheme-year boundaries must be preserved.
A regulatory reporting obligation is not itself an emissions measurement for an unrelated site or parcel.

packages.title: UK ETS maritime first-surrender QA
facts: UK ETS guidance states that allowances for the 2026 and 2027 maritime scheme years are first surrendered by 30 April 2028.
The first surrender aggregates the relevant emissions figures for those initial scheme periods.
An allowance surrender date is different from the date emissions occurred.
Allowances are compliance instruments and should not be treated as physical fuel quantities.
Registry or surrender information requires the regulated-entity boundary to be preserved.

packages.title: UK ETS installation 20MW scope QA
facts: UK ETS guidance covers regulated installation activities that produce greenhouse-gas emissions.
It includes combustion on a site where combustion units have total rated thermal input above 20 MW, subject to scheme rules and exclusions.
Thermal-input threshold is an eligibility boundary rather than a measured emissions quantity.
An installation boundary may span differently from a cadastral parcel boundary.
Threshold eligibility cannot be used to infer a parcel emissions value.

packages.title: UK ETS Northern-Ireland electricity boundary QA
facts: UK ETS participation guidance states that Northern Ireland electricity generators remain in the EU ETS under the Ireland/Northern Ireland Protocol.
This creates a scheme-boundary distinction within UK energy activities.
UK-wide electricity statistics therefore cannot assume one ETS regime for every generator.
Regulatory scheme membership is distinct from physical generation and emissions quantities.
Scheme boundary must be retained before joining registry and emissions data.

packages.title: UK ETS 2026 allocation-period guard QA
facts: The installation compliance guidance was updated on 9 February 2026.
The update notes that the 2026 allocation period is treated separately from preceding and subsequent allocation periods.
The update also reflects the new METS IT system and revised compliance processes.
Allocation-period rules must not be backfilled across years without checking the applicable guidance.
Free-allocation rules do not create a measured parcel emissions value.

packages.title: ONS LCREE 2024 survey-estimate QA
facts: ONS released Low carbon and renewable energy economy, UK: 2024 on 25 February 2026.
The bulletin estimates UK LCREE turnover at £77.0 billion in 2024.
It estimates LCREE employment at 304,000 full-time equivalents in 2024.
The estimates are survey-based rather than a census of every business.
Economic turnover and employment are not greenhouse-gas emissions quantities.

packages.title: ONS LCREE confidence-interval QA
facts: ONS reports confidence intervals for LCREE survey estimates.
The bulletin explains that confidence intervals express statistical accuracy for survey-based estimates.
The survey samples businesses rather than observing the whole population.
Central estimates should therefore retain uncertainty context.
Survey confidence does not establish parcel-level identity or emissions.

packages.title: ONS LCREE sector-group boundary QA
facts: ONS groups LCREE activity into defined low-carbon and renewable-energy sectors.
The 2024 bulletin reports low-carbon electricity as the largest turnover group.
Energy-efficient products account for a large share of LCREE employment.
These groups describe economic activity rather than measured greenhouse-gas abatement.
Sector-group turnover cannot be converted directly into parcel emissions.

packages.title: LCREE indirect statistics-in-development QA
facts: ONS publishes indirect LCREE turnover and employment estimates separately from direct survey estimates.
The indirect estimates are official statistics in development.
The 2024 indirect estimates use 2023 input-output analytical tables.
ONS states that 2024 indirect estimates are provisional and notes potential double-counting bias.
Indirect economic estimates must not be treated as observed greenhouse-gas emissions.

packages.title: LCREE revision-history QA
facts: ONS LCREE datasets preserve previous versions and revision history.
Scheduled updates and revisions can supersede earlier data files.
Method changes can also cause revisions in indirect-estimate datasets.
A superseded economic estimate should not be silently reused as the current value.
Revision provenance must be retained in any derived candidate.

packages.title: CCC 2026 statutory-progress report QA
facts: The Climate Change Committee published its 2026 progress report to Parliament on 24 June 2026.
The report was laid before Parliament under section 36(1) of the Climate Change Act 2008.
It covers UK territorial emissions and progress toward emissions targets.
It also assesses policy progress and delivery indicators.
A statutory progress assessment is evidence about national policy and sector progress, not a parcel measurement.

packages.title: CCC pathway-versus-observation QA
facts: The CCC 2026 report discusses the Carbon Budget and Growth Delivery Plan pathway.
It considers sectoral contributions to that pathway.
It explicitly addresses uncertainties in the pathway.
Pathway values and policy targets are distinct from observed emissions.
National pathways must not be assigned to individual parcels as measured outcomes.

packages.title: RTFO 2025 fourth-provisional release QA
facts: DfT published the fourth provisional RTFO 2025 release on 13 May 2026.
The release covers renewable-fuel supply for January to December 2025 using data available as of 27 April 2026.
DfT states that the dataset is incomplete.
The complete finalised 2025 dataset is scheduled for November 2026.
Provisional RTFO figures must not be labelled final.

packages.title: RTFO sustainable-aviation-fuel exclusion QA
facts: DfT states that Sustainable Aviation Fuel is excluded from the RTFO statistics series from the 2025 obligation year.
SAF is instead reported under the separate SAF Mandate statistics.
RTFO coverage therefore changes at the 2025 boundary.
Aviation renewable fuel should not be added to RTFO totals after 2024 without checking the separate mandate source.
Policy-series coverage changes must be preserved before trend comparisons.

packages.title: RTFO certificate-versus-fuel QA
facts: The RTFO release reports amounts of renewable and fossil road-transport fuel.
It also reports Renewable Transport Fuel Certificates issued for eligible fuel.
It reports certificate balances and trades between suppliers and traders.
Certificate counts or trades are regulatory instruments rather than physical fuel quantities.
Certificates cannot be converted directly into parcel greenhouse-gas emissions.

packages.title: Bus 2025 revised-activity statistics QA
facts: DfT revised the year-ending-March-2025 annual bus statistics on 24 March 2026.
The revision reflected updated operator data and a processing enhancement.
DfT reports that revised passenger journeys changed by about 0.3% and vehicle mileage by about 0.6% at national level.
Passenger journeys and mileage are transport-activity metrics.
Bus activity statistics are not direct greenhouse-gas measurements.

packages.title: Road-freight 2025 activity QA
facts: DfT published accredited Road freight statistics: 2025 on 27 May 2026.
The release reports 1.53 billion tonnes of goods lifted by GB-registered HGVs operating in the UK.
It reports 162 billion tonne-kilometres moved.
It reports 19.0 billion vehicle-kilometres travelled.
Tonnes, tonne-kilometres and vehicle-kilometres are activity metrics and require separate fuel or emissions factors for greenhouse-gas estimation.

packages.title: Cross-source activity-to-parcel emissions guard QA
facts: Smart-meter, charger, planning, forestry, agriculture, aviation, transport and low-carbon-economy sources use different units and boundaries.
UK ETS and RTFO sources add regulatory boundaries that are not equivalent to cadastral boundaries.
Counts, areas, economic values, project status, certificates and transport activity must remain distinct from measured emissions.
Combining official sources does not remove the need for compatible time, geography, unit and entity binding.
No source in this 098 batch supplies a verified measured greenhouse-gas value for an individual cadastral parcel.
